storyline.label: Gemini Argon
storyline.latest_title: [AINews] AI Engineer NYC: Gemini 4 Argon, Vals AI Benchmarks

prior_narrative.tldr: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sep 30 as its next frontier model. Latent Space framed it a day later as DeepMind's answer to Astra and Fable, with 1M output tokens, but only Fairwind Program users could try it.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Gemini 4 Argon went generally available on Oct 14, a day after reaching Google Cloud, with Latent Space noting that independent benchmarks such as CursorBench so far confirm Google's claims.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: GA plus Google Cloud availability means you can price and test Argon today, and early independent numbers match the launch claims; the 1M output limit matters for long agent runs.

status.detail: Announced Sep 30 with restricted access; Google Cloud availability and safety documentation followed Oct 13, and GA was reported Oct 14.

beats.headline: 1M output, but access limited to Fairwind Program users
Argon reaches Google Cloud and goes GA; robotics variant and safety write-up follow

open_questions: What pricing and rate limits apply to Gemini 4 Argon on Google Cloud?
Do independent evals beyond CursorBench hold up against Astra and Fable?
Is Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics available outside DeepMind partners?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Run a small eval of Argon on Google Cloud against your pinned Gemini model and record cost per completed task before changing any default; check your own workload, since the independent confirmations so far are benchmark-based.

day_captions.1dc99b611b2499a3: DeepMind's account of how Argon was developed responsibly and safely.
